items.title: THE WAR OF WORRY — AND WHAT CONFIRMED IT
items.author: Aeon Nimbus Research
items.description: A US-led war killed a supreme leader. Equities melted up to record highs. The largest IPO in history priced into the noise — then wiped $927 billion in three sessions.
items.content:
Global Macro — A Late-Cycle Melt-Up

On 28 February 2026, US and Israeli forces launched nearly 900 strikes against Iran in twelve hours, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz — through which a fifth of the world’s oil passes — collapsing tanker traffic by more than ninety percent and threatening a second European energy crisis. Over the four months since, the conflict expanded across the Levant, the Caucasus, and the Gulf before a fragile ceasefire was signed on 17 June. Through all of it, global equities did not fall. They melted up to record highs. This note is not a prediction of imminent collapse. It is an argument about positioning: that a market which reprices the killing of a head of state and the closure of the world’s most important oil chokepoint as a dip-buying opportunity is exhibiting a late-cycle signature that warrants caution, not celebration.

01 THE ARGUMENT IN BRIEF

Three independent observations point to the same conclusion. First, the war of worry: markets have trained themselves to buy every geopolitical dip, a reflex that works precisely until it doesn’t. Second, the everything-rally: twelve-month returns were positive across nearly every major index worldwide — the kind of indiscriminate gain that rewards complacency over discipline. Third, the apex signal: a two-trillion-dollar IPO for a company that lost five billion dollars last year, priced into a live war, is the sort of liquidity euphoria found near cycle tops. House View — Late-Cycle. The melt-up is real and may extend — momentum is a force and we do not fight it blindly — but the risk/reward of chasing beta here is poor. This note favours raising quality, trimming the most stretched winners into strength, holding optionality for a correction, and treating SpaceX-style IPO euphoria as a sentiment marker rather than a participation invitation.

02 WHAT THIS NOTE IS NOT

It is not a crash call with a date attached. Markets can remain irrational, and stretched valuations can stretch further for quarters. The Shiller P/E sat above 30 for years before 2000 finally broke. A late-cycle stance is a probabilistic tilt toward caution and quality, not a binary bet on a top. Anyone reading this as “sell everything” has misread it. The correct posture is to stay invested but stop paying up.

03 THE THREE PILLARS — AT A GLANCE

The Timeline of Indifference

The defining market behaviour of 2026 is the speed with which geopolitical shock is absorbed and discarded. Each escalation in the Iran war produced a sharp, brief risk-off move — and each was bought within days. The pattern became so reliable that by June, headlines that would once have triggered multi-week drawdowns barely registered as intraday noise.

04 IRAN WAR TIMELINE & MARKET RESPONSE

05 WHY THE REFLEX EXISTS — AND WHY IT IS DANGEROUS

The dip-buying reflex is not irrational in isolation. It has been trained by fifteen years of policy backstops and by the specific observation that, in this cycle, every geopolitical selloff has reversed. Investors who bought each Iran-war dip were rewarded. The problem is structural: a reflex that has never been punished becomes consensus, and consensus positioning is fragile. When everyone has learned that dips are for buying, there is no marginal buyer left to catch the dip that doesn’t bounce. The energy channel remains the live risk. The UAE’s national oil company estimates full Hormuz flows will not resume until 2027 even with a deal, and European gas storage entered the conflict at roughly 30% capacity. A breakdown of the fragile June ceasefire would reintroduce an oil and inflation shock into a market that has priced essentially none of it.

The Tell: When a market stops reacting to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the issue is not that the news stopped mattering. It is that the market has stopped pricing risk. Those are very different things, and only one of them is sustainable.

Investing Was Darts THE TWO MARKETS · AI STOCKS VS. SOURCES OF FUNDS

There are currently 2 markets: (1) The AI stocks; (2) The sources of funds to buy the AI stocks. Earnings do matter for AI-themed stocks — but for the rest of the Technology universe, earnings really don’t matter YTD. Non-AI names with strong earnings growth are being sold to fund AI positions, creating a structural bifurcation between fundamentals and price action.

06 AI STOCKS VS. SOURCES OF FUNDS — STOCK MOVE VS. EARNINGS CHANGE, % YTD

Major Global Indices — Trailing 12-Month Returns

07 THE BREADTH PROBLEM BENEATH THE RETURNS

The headline returns conceal a structural fragility: leadership is extraordinarily narrow. In Korea, SK Hynix and Samsung drive roughly half the index; BTIG noted the KOSPI rose 12% over six sessions in June while daily breadth was negative throughout. The same concentration defines the US, where AI mega-caps account for the majority of S&P 500 gains. Narrow leadership means the index level overstates the health of the average stock, and the downside is correlated: the same names that drove the melt-up would drive the unwind.

The Tell: When the consensus response to a 100% index gain is to forecast further upside, the burden of proof has quietly shifted from the bulls to the bears. That is a late-cycle hallmark.

SpaceX as the Apex Signal

THE LARGEST IPO IN HISTORY · LATE-CYCLE EUPHORIA · THE $927B UNWIND

DAY-1 MKT CAP $2.1T P/S (2025 REV) ~110× 2025 NET LOSS −$4.9B CAPITAL RAISED $75B OFF ATH (23 JUN) −31.3%

On 12 June 2026, SpaceX completed the largest IPO in history — raising approximately $75 billion at $135 per share, closing the first day at $160.95, a 19% pop that valued the company above $2 trillion. It is also, this note argued before the IPO priced, a textbook marker of late-cycle liquidity euphoria. What followed confirmed it.

08 SPCX PRICE — IPO TO POST-FILING COLLAPSE

09 THE CALL — ON THE RECORD, 9 JUNE 2026 — PUBLISHED BEFORE IPO PRICING

Published 9 June, three days before SpaceX IPO pricing: “Thursday and Friday, the market likely pumps — SPCX opens, retail flows in, the AI trade catches a bid. Then the week of June 16, I expect a broader correction. A $75B raise is capital pulled forward and locked up — historically, blockbuster IPOs mark short-term tops in the sectors that funded them.” — Aeon Nimbus Research, 9 June 2026

The Complication — A Hawkish Fed MONETARY POLICY · INFLATION · THE SETUP THIS CREATES

The melt-up has occurred despite, not because of, monetary policy — and that is the most underappreciated risk in the current setup. Markets entered 2026 pricing further rate cuts. They are exiting the first half facing the opposite. At the June meeting, the Federal Reserve under new Chair Kevin Warsh held the funds rate at 3.50– 3.75% and delivered a decisively hawkish message: nine of eighteen officials now pencil in at least one rate hike in 2026, with only one projecting a cut.

10 FED PROJECTIONS — MARCH VS JUNE 2026

11 THE SETUP THIS CREATES

Combine the pieces. Equities at record highs and a Shiller P/E of 42.8 — the second-highest reading in history, behind only the 44.2 of December 1999. A war-driven energy shock pushing inflation forecasts toward 3.6%. A central bank that has abandoned its easing bias, withdrawn forward guidance, and whose committee is split on whether to hike. Valuations expanded all year on the expectation of monetary easing that is no longer coming. That is the textbook definition of a multiple resting on a premise the data has since invalidated.

Policymakers raised their headline PCE inflation forecast substantially, driven by the energy shock from the Hormuz disruption. Retail sales rose a stronger-than-expected 0.9% in May, removing any near-term growth pretext for easing. The two-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in over a year following the meeting. Warsh declined to submit projections and said forward guidance is “no longer well suited” to the environment — removing the very predictability markets have leaned on. The Divergence: Stretched valuations require either accelerating earnings or falling discount rates to sustain. The war is pressuring earnings via energy costs, and the Fed is raising the discount rate via a hawkish hold. Both supports are weakening at once. That is the core of the late-cycle case.

Historical Context — What 42.8 Has Meant

Valuation is a poor timing tool and an excellent conditioning one. A high Shiller P/E does not tell you when the market will fall; it tells you that forward returns are likely to be lower and drawdowns deeper when they come. At 42.8, the cyclically-adjusted P/E sits at its second-highest level in the 150-year history of the series. The only higher reading preceded the dot-com collapse.

12 SHILLER P/E AT EXTREMES — HISTORICAL PRECEDENTS

13 THE 1999 PARALLEL — AND ITS CRUCIAL CAVEAT
The parallels to 1999 are the most direct: a transformative technology (AI now, the internet then) with genuine long-term merit, a market concentrated into a handful of names embodying that technology, a wave of richly-valued IPOs culminating in a marquee listing, and a consensus that valuation no longer applies because the paradigm is new. The crucial caveat: the Shiller P/E first crossed 30 in mid-1997, and the market roughly doubled again before peaking in March 2000. Being early was indistinguishable from being wrong for nearly three years. That is exactly why this note argues for a tilt, not an exit.

14 THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, STATED FAIRLY

The AI capex cycle is real and is producing genuine earnings, not just narrative — unlike 1999, today’s leaders are extraordinarily profitable. Corporate balance sheets are robust. The Shiller P/E has structurally drifted higher over decades as accounting standards, sector composition (more asset-light software), and lower long-run rates have changed what “normal” means. A constructive investor would argue the melt-up reflects real productivity gains and that the Fed’s hawkishness simply reflects a strong economy. If the ceasefire holds, the single largest tail risk is removed.

These are serious points. This note weighs them and still lands on caution — because the asymmetry of paying 42.8× into a hawkish hike-leaning Fed and a live energy shock is unfavourable, regardless of how good the underlying businesses are.

Post-Mortem — The $927B Unwind

SPACEX DEBT FILING · PREDICTED VS ACTUAL · IPO BUYER BREAKDOWN CLOSING ATH (16 JUN) $211 OFF ATH (23 JUN) −31.3% SPCX (23 JUN) $154.60 MKT CAP WIPED $927B DEBT FILED (22 JUN) $20B

SpaceX raised $75 billion in the largest IPO in history. Six days later, it filed for $20 billion in debt. The aspiration didn’t change. The capital need became quantifiable, and the market re-priced accordingly. This section documents the data that confirmed the 9 June call and what the sequence tells us about where markets go from here.

15 PREDICTED VS. ACTUAL — DAY BY DAY

16 IPO BUYER BREAKDOWN — WHO IS SITTING ON WHAT

The market re-priced not because the business became worse. It re-priced because the capital intensity became quantifiable. At $10B per quarter in capex, the entire $75B IPO raise is consumed in less than two years. The $20B debt filing was the first time a fundamental constraint imposed itself on the aspiration.

Credit Markets & The Other Side

AI CAPEX SUPPLY WAVE · CONTRARIAN PORTFOLIO · SPLIT MARKET 17 THE $20B DEBT FILING — A CREDIT MARKET EVENT

High-yield spreads at 278 basis points and investment-grade spreads at 25-year tights were priced for almost no disruption. SpaceX’s $20 billion bond offering — the largest debut corporate bond issuance in years — landed into that market on the same day as its equity unwind. The supply wave was a forward-looking risk flagged in this note’s original macro thesis. SpaceX moved it from forward to present in a single filing.

18 THE CONTRARIAN PORTFOLIO — THE OTHER SIDE OF THE MARKET

The most interesting asymmetry in this market is not where the momentum is — it is where it isn’t. A set of high-quality businesses are down 25–50% from their 12-month highs while still printing record revenues, earnings, and free cash flow. These are not broken companies. They are companies that have become the source of funds for the AI trade, and in that process their valuations have compressed to levels that price in disruption that has not yet appeared in any of the numbers.

This is a watchlist, not a buy list — timing a mean reversion against momentum is difficult. But when the AI trade eventually rotates, these are the names I expect to lead the recovery. Luxury at the worst sentiment in years. Adobe and Booking punished on AI disruption fears not yet visible in bookings. Uber pressured on autonomous vehicle speculation. Visa and Mastercard near decade-low multiples on businesses growing double-digits with near-100% margins. Netflix down 45% YTD on a business that is executing. Alibaba in correction despite re-accelerating earnings. The market is pricing deterioration that has not arrived in the fundamentals. That is the definition of a setup.

The Split Market: KOSPI +190% over 12 months. Netflix −45%. Visa near decade-low multiples. The index number is a weighted average of very different experiences. That divergence is the clearest evidence yet that the market is one trade dressed as 500 stocks.

Cross-Asset Positioning — H2 2026 STANCE & REASONING · FOUR SCENARIOS · THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT IDEA

19 H2 2026 SCENARIOS — FOUR PATHS, SKEWED DISTRIBUTION

The Single Most Important Idea: The cost of caution is currently low and the cost of complacency is currently high. Protection is cheap because volatility is suppressed. The melt-up has made defensive positioning unusually inexpensive at the exact moment the case for it is unusually strong — a rare configuration that does not require predicting a top to act on.

Sources & References PRIMARY & NAMED SOURCES · CONSOLIDATED EDITION, ISSUE 02

All analysis and position calls are the analyst’s own independent judgement, timestamped before outcomes were known.

items.title: MARVELL TECHNOLOGY
items.author: Aeon Nimbus Research
items.description: Jensen Huang calls it the next trillion-dollar company. Wall Street's consensus target sits below the current price.
items.content:
Thesis

Marvell Technology is almost certainly one of the most important semiconductor companies of the AI era — embedded in every major hyperscaler's custom chip programme, holding a structural duopoly with Broadcom in a market growing toward $100 billion, and freshly anointed by Jensen Huang as the next trillion-dollar company. And yet its stock, at the time of this report, is being sold aggressively — not because the thesis has broken, but because the largest IPO in capital market history is absorbing institutional liquidity tomorrow. The selling pressure has a hard end date. The structural bid arriving June 22 does not.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) designs semiconductor solutions for data infrastructure, spanning data center, carrier, enterprise networking, consumer, and automotive markets. The company is fabless — manufacturing is outsourced primarily to TSMC on advanced nodes (5nm, 3nm) — and operates as a pure-play designer of highcomplexity, high-margin silicon.

The company has undergone a structural transformation over the past four years, shedding commodity businesses (automotive ethernet divested to Infineon for $2.5B in August 2025) and consolidating around AI data infrastructure through four landmark acquisitions: Inphi (high-speed optical), Cavium (data processing), Celestial AI ($3.25B, February 2026, photonic fabric), and XConn Technologies (February 2026, chiplet connectivity). Data center revenue now represents 76% of the total, up from ~35% in FY2022

REVENUE SEGMENTATION — Q1 FY27

KEY STRATEGIC DEVELOPMENTS — LAST 12 MONTHS

MACRO CONTEXT — THREE RAILS

MRVL's investment case runs on three rails: an AI capex cycle that is accelerating rather than plateauing; a US rate environment that is modestly accommodative without being stimulative; and a geopolitical landscape that — despite its complexity — structurally advantages US-aligned fabless designers over any reasonable medium-term horizon. The five major hyperscalers are on track to spend approximately $520 billion in capital expenditure in 2026, a ~30% increase over 2025's record $400 billion. Custom silicon reduces per-token inference costs by 30–60% versus general-purpose GPUs for specific workloads, creating a durable economic incentive for hyperscalers to commit multi-year design budgets — which is precisely where MRVL's XPU programmes sit.

SPACEX IPO NEXUS — ROTATION MECHANICS & ENTRY WINDOW

SpaceX (SPCX) is set to price on the evening of 11 June 2026, with first trading on 12 June. At a reported $135 per share implying a $1.75 trillion valuation and a $75 billion raise — the largest IPO in stock market history — this event is absorbing institutional liquidity across the entire technology complex this week. MRVL is down approximately 11.4% on 10 June, from a post-inclusion high of ~$289 on 8 June. This drawdown is not fundamental: Q1 FY27 earnings beat consensus, Q2 guidance was raised, FY28 guidance was revised up 10% to $16.5B two weeks ago, and NVIDIA's CEO called Marvell the next trillion-dollar company at Computex just seven days ago. The selling is institutional cash-raising ahead of SPCX allocation, compounded by Alphabet's $84.75 billion equity raise — the largest share offering on record — which priced on 2 June and pulled significant capital out of the technology complex in the same window. Since that date, the Magnificent Seven have collectively shed approximately $2 trillion in market value, accounting for more than two-thirds of the S&P 500's total drawdown over the period. MRVL's pullback is part of that same mechanical compression, not a reflection of anything in its own business.

SpaceX IPO — base case sequence

The analyst's base case for the SPCX sequence is more specific than the four-scenario table suggests. The most likely outcome is not a clean success or a clean failure — it is a short-lived pump followed by a market-level correction in the week of June 16.

The $190 stop is sized to survive this sequence. If the June 16–20 correction pushes MRVL below $190, the broader market thesis has broken — not just MRVL. In that scenario, exiting is correct regardless of June 22. If the correction stays above $190, the June 22 inclusion bid arriving into a dip is actually a more powerful setup than a clean recovery would be.

Reading the $245.05 entry context - MOMENTUM ENTRY WITH FUNDAMENTAL ANCHOR

This entry at $245.05 on 9 June needs to be read clearly: it comes after a parabolic run, with MRVL up approximately 298% from its 52-week low of $61.44. The stock is not cheap, and the 11% pullback from the $289 post-inclusion spike is not a value reset — it is a mechanical bleed caused by SpaceX allocation cash-raising. Anyone treating this as a distressed entry is misreading the setup.

There is a meaningful distinction between buying a hyped stock that has run on narrative alone and buying a genuinely exceptional business at elevated prices with specific near-term catalysts. MRVL falls in the latter category. The company is producing record revenue today. Its $75 billion design win pipeline extends visibility into FY29–30. The custom silicon relationships with Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are multi-generational — switching costs are so high that a hyperscaler who commits to a Marvell XPU programme effectively commits for three to five chip generations. The NVIDIA partnership is technically embedded, not promotional. The Celestial AI optical franchise addresses what is genuinely the next constraint in AI cluster architecture. These are not narrative assets — they are contracted revenue.

The premium to DCF fair value (~$81/share) reflects the market pricing that multi-year revenue trajectory in advance. Whether that premium is 'too high' is a separate question from whether the business quality justifies a sustained premium at all. It does. The entry is timed to a specific catalyst window — not blind momentum-chasing — but it sits on top of a genuine, compounding fundamental case that runs well beyond June 22.

Financial analysis — Q1 FY27 record quarter

REVENUE & EPS PROJECTION MODEL

BALANCE SHEET — Q1 FY27

WACC construction

FIVE-YEAR DCF — DISCOUNTING FREE CASH FLOW, NOT NARRATIVE

DCF SENSITIVIT Y — INTRINSIC VALUE PER SHARE (WACC ↓ / TERMINAL GROWTH →)

Reverse DCF — what $245 requires

The reverse DCF inverts the question: given the $245.05 entry (EV ~$220B), what terminal economics must the market be assuming? At a 13.73% WACC and 4% terminal growth, the implied terminal FCF is ~$20.6B — reached only if the $10B+ FY29 XPU programme, optical attach, and networking expansion compound on schedule through FY32–33.

PROBABILIT Y-WEIGHTED PAYOFF — 12-MONTH HORIZON FROM $245.05

Competitive positioning — structural duopoly MRVL & AVGO HOLD NEAR-TOTAL SHARE OF HYPERSCALER ASIC DESIGN

The custom AI silicon market is a structural duopoly. Broadcom (AVGO) and Marvell (MRVL) collectively hold near-total share of hyperscaler ASIC design programmes, with Broadcom commanding approximately 70% market share anchored by its long-running Google TPU programmes and a 5-year supply commitment formalised in April 2026. Marvell holds the remaining ~30% with Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia, and an emerging Google MPU co-development programme.

NVLINK FUSION PARTNERSHIP — STRATEGIC MOAT

The March 31 NVIDIA partnership deserves emphasis beyond its financial terms. NVLink Fusion creates a technical architecture where Marvell's custom XPUs are natively compatible with NVIDIA's GPU ecosystem — meaning hyperscalers building mixed NVIDIA/custom silicon infrastructure naturally route custom ASIC design work to Marvell. The $2B equity stake backs it at the silicon level, not the marketing level. Jensen Huang's comment at Computex — calling Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' — should be read as a competitive signal: NVIDIA is aligning with the ASIC player most likely to complement rather than threaten its ecosystem, and validating that choice in front of 1,500 institutional investors.

DESIGN WIN PIPELINE — $75B LIFETIME REVENUE FUNNEL

Marvell has disclosed 18+ confirmed XPU and XPU-attach socket design wins, many already in volume production. The total design win pipeline encompasses more than 50 opportunities with a $75 billion lifetime revenue funnel. These wins span full custom XPU programmes, XPU-attached silicon (memory, I/O), electrical chiplets integrated inside multi-die packages, and optical interconnect. Even partial conversion — say, 10–15% of the $75B lifetime value annually — supports the $10B+ FY29 revenue guidance. Design wins have multi-year revenue visibility once a hyperscaler commits to a generation of custom silicon; switching costs are extraordinarily high.

The hyperscaler capex cycle is compressing into a narrower set of beneficiaries than the market appreciates. Alphabet raised $84.75 billion in a single equity offering on 2 June — the largest share offering in history — specifically to fund AI compute infrastructure, with Berkshire Hathaway anchoring $10 billion of it in a concurrent private placement. Meta is evaluating a comparable equity raise of tens of billions, with its own AI capex guidance now running at $125–145 billion for 2026 alone. Capital deployed at this scale routes to custom silicon, purpose-built interconnect, and co-packaged optics. Marvell sits at the intersection of all three.

Three variant views

Institutional ownership & analyst consensus

Major asset managers Vanguard and BlackRock increased their MRVL positions during Q1 2026, as the NVIDIA strategic investment provided institutional validation of the AI thesis. NVIDIA's own $2B equity stake is a notable addition to the shareholder register — a strategic investor with strong informational asymmetry who chose to buy, not partner. The spread between Morningstar's $123 DCF fair value and Stifel's $321 market-multiple target captures the central tension: an exceptional business priced at a level that only makes sense if the AI build-out sustains 40%+ revenue growth for years.

DATED CATALYST WATCHLIST

Risk factors — six genuine risks

Position statement

The thesis and all parameters were established before the position was initiated. Closing posts will reference this document as the original record. Positions are never selectively disclosed — this report constitutes the full public record at time of entry.

items.title: REDDIT INC - Not AI's victim — its feedstock.
items.author: Aeon Nimbus Research
items.description: The internet's authentic human archive, mispriced as a social network.
items.content:
Thesis
A business that grew net income 685% year-on-year is priced as though it is decelerating into irrelevance. Reddit's stock is down 41% year to date. In the same period, the company reported $663 million in quarterly revenue growing 69%, a 91.5% gross margin, $312 million in operating cash flow, and $1 million in capital expenditure. The dislocation has a specific cause: the market is reading RDDT against social media comparables. The correct frame is a data licensing counterparty to every major large language model developer on earth. Those are categorically different businesses. The former deserves a Pinterest multiple. The latter has no comparable precedent.

The non-consensus claim is precise: authenticated human discourse at scale is the scarcest input in the AI training economy, Reddit owns the largest open-market repository of it, and the pricing model for that asset is transitioning from flat-rate contracts toward dynamic value-based structures. None of that is in the consensus. All of it is already happening.

SCENARIO ANALYSIS

INVALIDATION CONDITIONS

REVENUE BRIDGE — FY2025 ACTUAL TO FY2027E BASE ($M)

Macro context — investment backdrop

The macro regime is constructive for internet advertising but carries a specific complication for RDDT: the US 10-year yield at 4.98% raises the discount rate applied to growth-phase cash flows, compressing the multiple that a forward-looking DCF would assign to FY2027 earnings. That compression is already visible in the stock — down 41% year to date against a fundamental business that has accelerated, not deteriorated. The dislocation is not macro-driven. It is a re-rating of social media multiples following Meta Forum's launch, combined with insider selling optics and a UK regulatory fine. None of these events have altered the earnings trajectory.

BUSINESS MODEL OVERVIEW — THREE INTERLOCKING REVENUE STREAMS

Reddit operates three interlocking revenue streams. Advertising — the dominant engine at $625M in Q1 2026, growing 74% year-on-year — monetises the commercial intent embedded in roughly 40% of platform conversations. AI data licensing monetises the 20-year archive of authenticated human discourse that large language model developers cannot replicate. Commerce and other revenues — $38M in Q1 — include Shopify-integrated dynamic product ads and early social commerce infrastructure. The three streams reinforce each other: more users generate more data, which generates more licensing revenue, which funds the product investment that retains users.

COMMERCIAL INTENT & AD CONVERSION BY COMMUNITY VERTICAL — Q1 2026E

Financial overview — the SEC-verified record

The capital structure is exceptional for a platform at this scale: $2.8B in cash and investments, no meaningful debt, $1M quarterly capex, and a $1B share repurchase programme authorised in February 2026. Reddit does not need the capital markets. It is beginning to return capital to shareholders at 18 months post-IPO.

WACC CONSTRUCTION — BUILT FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES

Reddit carries no meaningful debt. The WACC is effectively the cost of equity. The construction below uses the CAPM framework anchored to the current 10-year Treasury at 4.98%.

A 12.4% WACC applied to a business growing at 44–69% with 91% gross margins and 47% operating cash flow margins is conservative by construction. The sensitivity analysis tests whether the thesis survives at 14% — the upper bound of the plausible range for this risk profile.

DCF model — five-year base case

FY2026E $3,050M anchored to H1 actuals: Q1 $663M + Q2 guided midpoint $720M = $1,383M; H2 ~$1,667M at modest sequential growth. Sum of PV (FCF 2026–2030) ≈ $6,770M. Terminal value at 20× FY2030 EBITDA = $67,000M, discounted 5 years at 12.4% ≈ $37,407M. Enterprise value ≈ $44,177M. Net cash add-back $2,800M. Equity value ≈ $46,977M. Implied per share (~190M diluted): ~$247. Base case uses 10× EV/FY2027E Rev = ~$182.

SENSITIVITY MATRIX — IMPLIED SHARE PRICE

Entry $140.88 is below every cell in this matrix at 9× or higher — intrinsic value at base WACC and a below-consensus revenue multiple. Stop $122 maps to the 7× / 14% cell: the point at which the fundamental thesis has broken down, not merely repriced.

COMPARABLE COMPANY ANALYSIS

The 2030 model — three paths

The 2030 bear case at $222 implies +57% from entry. Even a scenario in which every growth lever underperforms consensus produces a double from current price over a four-year horizon. The base case at $399 (+183%) requires no assumptions beyond the business delivering on its published guidance trajectory.

BETA CONTEXT — RDDT VS S&P 500

The stated β of 1.35 (2-year weekly OLS) reflects the idiosyncratic volatility profile of a post-IPO growth stock. Each monthly point in the 24-month window (Mar 2024–Apr 2026) carries large residual variance against the index — the regression line passes through a cloud, not a corridor. As RDDT matures and price volatility normalises, beta will trend toward the platform peer average of ~1.0, compressing the discount rate and expanding the intrinsic value range.

Why β = 1.35 is itself conservative. The 2-year regression window captures Reddit's most volatile period — IPO through licensing repricing through Meta Forum reaction. Each successive quarter of profitable, recurring revenue compresses idiosyncratic variance. At β = 1.0, ceteris paribus, WACC drops to 10.48%; the base-case DCF crosses $240 without any change in revenue or margin assumptions.

Read-through. The sensitivity matrix on the prior page already tests WACC down to 10.5%. The implied price at 10.5% / 10× is $223. Beta compression is therefore not a separate bull lever — it is the mechanical pathway by which the base-case multiple expands as Reddit ages out of post-IPO classification.

AI data licensing — the moat, the contracts, the transition

Twenty years of community-generated content represents an asset that cannot be reconstructed from scratch. The time dimension alone is prohibitive: no new platform can produce 2010-era human discourse in 2026. That temporal irreplaceability — combined with community authentication, upvote-validated accuracy, and the explicit commercial intent embedded in a large proportion of threads — positions Reddit's corpus as the single most valuable training dataset on the open market for large language model developers.

"Authenticated human discourse at scale is the scarcest input in the AI training economy. Reddit owns the largest open-market repository of it."

THE CONTRACT STACK — KNOWN AND ESTIMATED

PRICING TRANSITION — FLAT → USAGE → DYNAMIC

The global AI datasets and licensing market: $382 million in 2024, projected at $1.59 billion by 2030 at a 26.8% CAGR (Grand View Research). Reddit's current ~$140M in Other revenue represents roughly 37% of the entire 2024 market — before Phase 2 and Phase 3 pricing structures are negotiated. The ceiling on this revenue stream is not visible from current contracts.

Investment thesis — three pillars

Three independent re-rating levers, each with its own evidence base and its own falsification test. The position does not require all three to fire — base case requires only the first two. Any single lever fully delivered justifies the entry price.

Variant views — consensus vs Aeon Nimbus

Three sell-side positions disagree with our view at named price targets. Each is treated as a falsifiable counter-thesis with an explicit test condition. The case for the position is strongest when the variant views can be specified precisely enough to be wrong.

Reverse DCF — what $140.88 requires the market to believe

Rather than ask what Reddit is worth, the reverse DCF asks: at entry $140.88 (~$27B market cap), what must the market believe about growth and margins for this price to be fair? If those implied beliefs are pessimistic relative to what the business currently delivers, the stock is cheap.

PAYOFF ASYMMETRY AT ENTRY $140.88

INSTITUTIONAL OWNERSHIP — THE DISCOVERY PHASE

Reddit listed in March 2024. At 26 months public the register is structurally incomplete: 896 filers hold 128M shares. Top-five holders all filed passive 13G disclosures in the last 90 days. Baillie Gifford added 1.33M shares at $134.65 on March 31, 2026 — a +22% position increase at prices near current entry. Active accumulation by a long-duration compounder, not passive index drift. The discovery phase is named dated priced.

items.title: IREN LIMITED - The Power Is the Moat.
items.author: Aeon Nimbus Research
items.description: The Market Is Still Pricing the Miner.
items.content:
Thesis — the gap is the investment

IREN has $13.1 billion in signed contracts with Microsoft and NVIDIA. Sweetwater 1 — 1.4 GW — was energised on schedule on May 1. Childress is an active construction site with a Q3 Microsoft handoff in scope. The stock closed at $47.88 on May 19, down 37.8% from its 52-week high, because screeners read a GAAP net loss and a 38.5% share-count expansion, not a yield upgrade from $1.5M/MW to $9.7M/MW on the same power infrastructure. The gap between what IREN is and what the market thinks it is remains the investment

SCENARIO ANALYSIS

THESIS INVALIDATED IF

  • Horizon 1 commissioning delayed beyond Q4 CY2026 with confirmed Microsoft timeline miss.

  • ATM tapping above $2B in 90 days without any new signed contract.

  • Hyperscaler CapEx guidance cut 15%+ — CoreWeave, AWS, Azure all guide down simultaneously.

  • NVIDIA renegotiates or cancels $3.4B contract or warrant.

Macro context · 20 May 2026. S&P 500 at all-time highs · 30Y above 5% · Iran ceasefire deteriorating · April CPI 3.8% · Warsh in his first week as Fed chair. None of these affect the investment. Revenue is contractually locked in 5-year take-or-pay agreements with Microsoft ($9.7B) and NVIDIA ($3.4B). The relevant macro figure is the $715B in global hyperscaler CapEx commitments for 2026 — growing, not shrinking. At 4.98% on the 10Y our WACC rises modestly to 13.5%; the adjustment shifts base case DCF by $3.

Near-term event flag. NVIDIA reports Q1 FY2027 earnings tonight after market close, 20 May 2026. NVIDIA is simultaneously IREN's GPU supplier, its second-largest revenue counterparty ($3.4B contract), and a potential equity stakeholder via the 30M-share warrant at $70. Any guidance on Blackwell GB300 supply-chain health, DSX partner buildout pace, or AI infrastructure CapEx from hyperscaler clients directly affects IREN's near-term execution risk profile. We treat this as a sentiment and risk-calibration event, not a thesis event. Specific watch points are in the Catalyst Watchlist

Why power is the actual moat

The decline from $76.87 to $47.88 — a fall of 37.8% — was driven by a Q3 FY2026 GAAP net loss of $247.8M that screeners read as operational distress, a 38.5% YoY dilution that triggered automatic risk flags in quantitative models, and broader risk-off pressure in the small-cap AI infrastructure cohort through April May 2026. None describes the business.

IREN was founded in November 2018 by brothers Daniel and William Roberts on a thesis being validated in real time: the fundamental constraint on the digital economy is not software, not chips, not GPUs — it is power. Dependable, cheap, grid-connected, permitted electrical power at gigawatt scale. Everything else can be bought, financed, or hired. Power cannot be created on demand.

You can buy GPUs. You can finance racks. You can hire engineers overnight. You cannot create 1 GW of grid connected, permitted, energised power in Western markets in less than 4–7 years. IREN has secured more than 5 GW across six jurisdictions with grid agreements signed, permits resolved, and land owned.

At Sweetwater: 890+ hectares in Fisher County, ERCOT connection agreements with $4.1M in non-refundable costs already paid, fibre loops under 10ms latency to hyperscaler regions. Sweetwater 1 — 345kV/138kV, energised May 1, 2026, on schedule. This is the moat.

The build template is repeatable. Each subsequent phase benefits from the same design, supply chain, construction sequencing, and site team. Microsoft could not build the equivalent in the timeframe AI demand required. This is time-to-compute as a product, sold at $9.7B because there is no faster alternative.

"Microsoft was not simply seeking incremental expansion. They needed immediate compute capacity against physical power constraints inside Azure." DANIEL ROBERTS, CO-CEO · Q3 FY2026 EARNINGS CALL

THE CONTRACT STACK — $3.1B ARR AT 30 APRIL 2026

Financial overview — what the screeners miss

Q3 FY2026, ENDED 31 MARCH 2026

The Q3 print is the photograph of a yield upgrade mid-transition. $140.4M of the $247.8M loss is paper — the cost of retiring legacy ASICs to liberate the same MW for Microsoft AI Cloud. The accounting calls this destruction. The economics call it repricing $1.5M/MW power into $9.7M/MW power .

WACC construction BUILT FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES

FIVE-YEAR FINANCIAL MODEL — DISCOUNTING CONTRACTED REVENUE, NOT PROJECTIONS

TERMINAL VALUE — TWO METHODS, ONE ANSWER

Sensitivity matrix — implied price LONG IREN · $47.88 → $86 ROWS: WACC · COLUMNS: EV / EBITDA FY2030E

At entry $47.88 with 13.5% WACC, IREN prices at approximately 9–10× EV/EBITDA FY2030E — below the Cohort B floor of 11×. The market prices IREN below the weakest-cohort floor while it holds the highest-quality anchor contracts in the sector. At partial Cohort A re-rating (18×) the model implies $108. Our target $86 corresponds to ~14–15× — conservative by any peer standard.

PEER COMPARISON — EV/MW DISLOCATION

ROIC PER DEPLOYED MW — UNIT ECONOMICS

Revenue per MW at full Horizon deployment: ~$9.7M/year (Microsoft contract rate). Power cost per MW: $0.028–0.04/kWh × 8,760h × 1,000 kW = $245 350k/year. Gross cash margin per MW: ~$9.35 9.45M/year before debt service and G&A — an implied gross margin of 96–97% per MW.

For context, a standard hyperscaler operating at $0.07/kWh carries a power cost of $613k/MW/year, reducing their gross margin per MW by approximately $265–370k relative to IREN. At 810 MW operative today and a weighted average revenue mix of ~$4.0M/MW (BTC + early AI Cloud), IREN generates approximately $3.24B in gross cash before CapEx.

The ramp to $9.7M/MW per the Microsoft rate — which applies to 200 MW of Childress capacity — converts each redeployed MW into a sixfold gross cash uplift. This is the unit economic engine behind the financial model.

IREN trades at $23.1M/MW — 31% of CoreWeave's $74M/MW — on anchor client quality that is functionally equivalent. No other power-first operator carries both Microsoft and NVIDIA at investment-grade, 5-year take-or-pay terms. The re-rating gap closes when Horizon 1 delivers Q3 CY2026 and EBITDA turns positive in FY2027.

Investment thesis — three pillars LONG IREN · $47.88 → $86 WHAT THE MARKET IS MISPRICING

Pillar 1: 5+ GW of secured power is the only moat that cannot be replicated — it took IREN eight years.

A developer starting from scratch today would need: land in a low-cost power jurisdiction, signed interconnection agreements with grid operators, regulatory approvals, water and cooling rights, fibre connectivity, and then the actual physical construction. In most Western markets this takes 4–7 years. IREN has already done it across six jurisdictions.

Sweetwater 1 — 1.4 GW at 345kV/138kV, energised May 1, 2026, on schedule — is one of the largest single pieces of AI infrastructure energised anywhere in the world this year. IREN has been hitting milestones consistently: Prince George GPU deliveries commissioning, Mackenzie prepared for H2 2026 GPU installations, Childress Horizon 1 underway with 3,000 workers on site simultaneously.

The power is the moat. The build template is the engine.

Pillar 2: NVIDIA is not a customer — it is a strategic stakeholder with $2.1B of equity incentive above $70

The NVIDIA relationship has three components. The $3.4B revenue contract for 60 MW of air-cooled Blackwell GPU capacity is what the market prices. The 5 GW DSX-aligned strategic partnership explains why IREN receives preferential GPU allocations that Tier-2 AI cloud operators cannot access. The warrant for 30 million shares at $70 strike aligns NVIDIA’s financial incentives directly with IREN’s stock performance above $70.

JPMorgan correctly identified a circularity in the NVIDIA structure: NVIDIA provides capital that IREN uses to buy NVIDIA GPUs, making NVIDIA simultaneously GPU supplier, revenue customer, and equity stakeholder. We take the concern seriously. The reason it does not break the thesis is the spread arithmetic: IREN’s power cost of $0.028–0.04/kWh in Childress is 50–65% below the $0.06–0.08/kWh that standard hyperscaler jurisdictions carry. Even if NVIDIA extracted 15–20% higher GPU pricing in renegotiation, IREN’s per-MW economics remain materially better than a typical datacenter operator.

The warrant at $70 is out of the money at entry $47.88; its exercise requires IREN to succeed.

Pillar 3: The Q3 GAAP loss is accounting — dilution is directed at contracted demand, not operating burn.

The Q3 FY2026 GAAP net loss of $247.8 million was dominated by $140.4 million in non-cash impairments on decommissioned ASIC mining hardware. IREN is retiring legacy Bitcoin mining equipment generating $1.5–2M/MW/year to liberate the same power for Microsoft AI Cloud generating $9.7M/MW/year. The accounting records the retirement as an impairment. The economics record it as a capital reallocation from a 3× yield to a 6.5× yield on the same power.

Operating CF is positive $96M/quarter. The existing funding stack — $4.73B cash, $3.6B GPU facility, $1.94B Microsoft prepayment — covers 100% of Horizons 1–4 without the ATM. The May 2026 convertible includes capped call hedges at $110.30. Share-count growth was most aggressive during the initial infrastructure build raises of 2024–2025; with that asset base now in place and revenue ramping, marginal dilution per dollar of new value created is declining.

The peak dilution-to-value ratio is behind us.

CapEx coverage — funding-gap stress test

THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES WITHOUT

$10.65B of committed, available, or generated funding covers the $5.90B two-year build programme with a $4.75B surplus before touching the $5.32B ATM. IREN does not need new equity to complete Horizons 1–4.

THE 2030 MODEL — FIVE VARIABLES

Bull 6.5 GW assumes acceleration from ~50 MW/mo to ~120 MW/mo by 2027 via three-site parallel builds (Sweetwater 1, Oklahoma, Childress). Base 5.0 GW requires only sequential execution of the already-permitted pipeline.

Three variant views

WHERE CONSENSUS IS WRONG · HOW EACH IS FALSIFIED

REVERSE DCF — WHAT $47.88 REQUIRES THE MARKET TO BELIEVE

At $47.88, EV is approximately $18.8B. For this to be fair value at 13.5% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth, IREN must generate perpetual normalised EBITDA of ~$1.9B — implying it never deploys the 4.2 GW of secured power beyond 810 MW. All of the following must simultaneously fail: Horizons 1–4 miss schedule · ARR does not reach the already-funded $3.1B · Sweetwater attracts no new hyperscaler · the 5 GW pipeline converts at < 20% over four years. The market is pricing collective failure of everything already funded contracted and physically underway.

Materially better than the prior entry at $52.63 (+53%), reflecting additional dislocation without any deterioration in the thesis. Stop at $32 sits below the bear-case floor, at the level where the contractual delivery thesis is demonstrably broken rather than temporarily discounted. Sized at 3% — not ½ Kelly of 18% — because information asymmetry on Horizon 1 delivery has not yet resolved.

INSTITUTIONAL OWNERSHIP — Q4 2025 13F ANALYSIS

Total institutional ownership: 39.3% — approximately 25–40 percentage points below Cohort A peers (CoreWeave, Nebius at 60–80%). Goldman's +5.15M shares while co-leading IREN's GPU debt facility is the most analytically significant signal: Goldman had full due-diligence access to the balance sheet and chose to add equity simultaneously.

Risk table — calibrated, not dismissed

CATALYST WATCHLIST

Position statement

We took a position in IREN Limited (NASDAQ: IREN) at an entry price of $47.88 on May 19, 2026. Our price target is $86.00, representing +79.6% from entry, consistent with the convergence of two independent valuation methods: DCF at 11× EBITDA FY2030E ($57; with 25% re-rating premium on Horizon 1 delivery, $71) and EV/ARR at CoreWeave’s 11.3× applied to $3.7B ARR exit CY2026 ($90), alongside Macquarie’s Outperform target raised to $90 on May 11, 2026.

Stop is set at $32.00 — below the bear case price floor of $32–38, at the level where the contractual delivery thesis is demonstrably broken rather than temporarily discounted. Sized at 3% of portfolio: win/loss ratio 2.40×, probability-weighted EV +76%, ½ Kelly = 18%. Sized at 3% rather than ½ Kelly because information asymmetry on Horizon 1 has not resolved.

items.title: Adeia — The Toll Booth on the Layer Nobody Is Watching
items.author: Aeon Nimbus Research
items.description: The Korean Patent Office flagged it. The market hasn't. A $39M acquisition in 2015 is becoming the royalty stream beneath the entire AI hardware stack.
items.content:
Every conversation in AI hardware is about GPUs, memory bandwidth, and photonics. Adeia operates below all of that — on the bonding layer that physically connects every chip in every HBM stack being manufactured today. They hold the foundational patents. Samsung and SK Hynix cannot build HBM4 without them. The Korean Patent Office has said so publicly. The market is pricing the media licensing business with a grudging nod to semiconductor upside. We believe it has the order exactly reversed.

Scenario table

Defined by LiJie Guo, Aeon Nimbus Research, May 1, 2026 · Long at $30.00 · Scenarios driven by logic licence pipeline (NVIDIA, Intel, Apple, Broadcom), HBM4 royalty ramp timing, and Q1 2026 earnings outcome.

Invalidated if: Q1 2026 results show revenue below $85M with no new licence in pipeline commentary · No logic licence closes in 2026 and management gives no pipeline visibility in H1 calls · S&P credit rating downgraded below BB · HBM4 production volumes shift away from hybrid bonding (alternative technology gains fab adoption)

This thesis was not obvious until we studied the technical literature carefully. The AI hardware debate centres on GPUs, memory bandwidth, and increasingly on photonics and optical interconnect — the visible bottlenecks discussed in analyst reports. Adeia operates on the invisible layer beneath all of them: the physical bonding process that allows HBM stacks to be assembled, chiplets to be integrated, and advanced packaging to function at the pitch densities AI systems require. It is a toll booth nobody is discussing, built on foundational IP that the Korean Patent Office has explicitly identified as a strategic national dependency risk for Samsung and SK Hynix.

The business model

Adeia is an IP licensing company operating two structurally distinct verticals under one balance sheet. The media vertical — legacy patents from TiVo and Rovi covering content discovery, DVR functionality, recommendation engines, and streaming technology — is the cash cow that has funded the company’s existence and debt reduction since the 2022 spinoff from Xperi. The semiconductor vertical — built around the DBI® (Direct Bond Interconnect) portfolio acquired when Tessera Technologies bought Ziptronix in 2015 for $39 million — is the thesis.

The business model is structurally superior to any manufacturing business in the semiconductor supply chain. Adeia does not build fabs. It does not buy equipment. It does not manage yields. CapEx guidance for 2026: $2 million. Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin: 73%. Every dollar of incremental revenue from a new licence falls through to earnings with essentially no incremental cost. When AMD signed its multi-year IP licence in March 2026, Adeia’s cost of delivering on that agreement was the legal and negotiation overhead already embedded in its operating expense base.

The licensing model has two components. One-time fees paid at signing — typically $20–50M for a major logic licence. Recurring royalties paid on each chip shipped that incorporates the licensed technology. The recurring stream is what makes this thesis genuinely multi-year: once AMD commits to hybrid bonding architecture for its 3D V-Cache chiplets, every subsequent generation generates royalties. Once Samsung and SK Hynix convert their HBM production lines to hybrid bonding for HBM4, royalties compound with the AI hardware industry’s own growth.

The technical moat

Hybrid bonding is the direct copper-to-copper and dielectric-to-dielectric connection of two chips or wafers without solder bumps. The physics are non-negotiable: HBM4 requires stacking 16+ memory dies with interconnect pitches below 10 microns. Flip-chip with conventional microbumps operates above 40 microns and cannot reach the interconnect density HBM4 demands at acceptable yield. Beyond density: eliminating the solder layer eliminates the primary thermal barrier between stacked dies — critical when AI GPU racks already exceed 163kW and roadmaps project 600kW/rack by 2027. Hybrid bonding is not an option among several. At these specifications, it is the only known process path.

The DBI® technology originated at Ziptronix, a North Carolina company founded around 2000 by researchers recognised in the technical literature as the primary inventors of direct-bond interconnect. Sony first implemented DBI® commercially in the CMOS image sensor used in the Samsung Galaxy S7 in 2016. A decade later, over 60 million smartphones annually incorporate CIS with hybrid bonding, and the same fundamental technology is now the required process for HBM4 memory stacking.

The KnowMade 2024 hybrid bonding patent landscape report identifies TSMC, Adeia, and YMTC as the three global leaders in hybrid bonding IP. The Korean Patent Office issued a formal public analysis warning that Samsung and SK Hynix — together controlling approximately 85% of global HBM production — face strategic national dependency on foreign hybrid bonding patents, specifically identifying Adeia and TSMC as the holders. When a national regulatory body of the world’s dominant HBM producer warns formally about dependency on Adeia’s patents, the competitive moat is not theoretical. It is documented at the sovereign level.10

Financial overview

Analyst coverage — trajectory from $17 to $40 in four months

From $17 in December 2025 to $33 average and $40 high in four months. Four upgrades. No downgrades. Zero Sell ratings. The next meaningful upgrade requires Q1 earnings confirmation, a new logic licence, or Tier-1 initiation. None of those three has happened yet.

WACC

DCF model — 5-year UFCF, base case

One new major logic licence closes H2 2026. AMD recurring revenue builds. HBM4 royalty stream begins as a line item by FY2027. Media declines 5% annually. Semiconductor revenue grows from $26M (2025) toward $100M by FY2028. EBITDA margins normalise to 58–62% as litigation spend moderates after 2026.

Sum of PV FCFs: $849M · Terminal value (Gordon Growth, 3.5% terminal, 12.0% WACC): $3.63B → PV: $2.07B · Enterprise value: $2.92B · Less net debt ~$(290M) · Equity value: $2.63B · Shares: ~111M · Base DCF: $23.69/share. Note: base DCF is below current price — the market is already paying for optionality on logic licences. Bull case DCF at $100M semiconductor revenue + two new logic licences implies $38–42. The position at $30 requires materialising the base-to-bull transition.

Sensitivity — implied share price (WACC × terminal EV/EBITDA)

Entry at $30 corresponds to 12% WACC and ~13× EV/EBITDA — the multiple of a comparable IP licensing company before its AI infrastructure re-rating. Target $42 corresponds to 12% WACC and 17× EV/EBITDA — appropriate if two logic licences and HBM4 royalties confirm the re-rating thesis.

Peer comparison

Rambus is the most relevant comparable — semiconductor memory IP focus, currently ~16× EV/EBITDA. Adeia trades at a discount (~13×) despite higher EBITDA margins and structurally superior AI infrastructure exposure. The discount is explained entirely by the media business dragging the blended multiple. Sum-of-parts at Rambus multiples on the semiconductor segment alone implies $40+ per share.

Investment thesis

Pillar 1 of 3

The DBI® portfolio is the TSMC of hybrid bonding IP — and TSMC is not publicly investable at small-cap prices

The KnowMade 2024 patent landscape report identified three global leaders in hybrid bonding: TSMC, Adeia, and YMTC. TSMC is a $700 billion foundry where hybrid bonding patents are one capability among thousands. YMTC is Chinese and navigating US export controls. Adeia is the only US-listed company whose primary strategic value derives from the hybrid bonding patent portfolio. It is the most direct public market exposure to the IP layer beneath AI hardware.

The correct analogy is ARM Holdings before the market understood that the ARM instruction set would become the standard for mobile chips. ARM licensed foundational process IP to every chip designer for royalties per chip, generating near-100% gross margin revenue that compounded with the mobile ecosystem. Adeia’s DBI® has the same structural position — foundational process IP that every HBM4 manufacturer must incorporate, licensed for royalties on each unit produced, with near-zero cost of delivery. The difference: ARM’s TAM was billions of mobile devices per year at $5–20 each. Adeia’s TAM is AI hardware, where HBM4 units are measured in millions per year at $10,000+ per unit. The royalty rate per dollar of product value is structurally higher in high-value AI components than in commodity mobile chips.

The AMD deal signed March 9, 2026 is described by CEO Davis as “seminal” — not because AMD alone changes the financial picture, but because AMD is now documented proof-of-concept for what a major logic chiplet licence looks like. AMD’s 3D V-Cache in Ryzen and EPYC processors uses hybrid bonding for the SRAM-on-logic stacking that gives those products their performance advantage. Every generation of V-Cache that ships is a royalty event for Adeia. CEO Davis has explicitly indicated he expects 2nd and 3rd logic adopters in 2026–2027.2

Pillar 2 of 3

The 2026 guidance “decline” is a deliberate management conservatism — the real story is what happens when the pipeline converts

The surface reading of Adeia’s FY2026 guidance — $395M–$435M versus $443M in 2025 — is the most common objection to the thesis. The guidance implies negative year-over-year revenue growth. Every quantitative screen flags this as a declining business. Four analysts who cover it maintain Buy ratings anyway. The divergence between the guidance signal and analytical conviction is explained by one fact: management guides only what is contractually confirmed, and the three most important Q1 2026 developments — the AMD deal (March 9), the UMC expansion (March 11), and the DISH Network litigation (April 1) — were all announced after the February 23 guidance was issued and are none of them included in it.

The increase in litigation expense — $5–10M above 2025 levels — is the clearest signal in the guidance that management is acting more aggressively on patent enforcement. Adeia filed against DISH Network on April 1, one month after the AMD resolution. Davis has described the playbook explicitly: file suit, create negotiating leverage, resolve through long-term licensing. The same sequence produced the Disney deal. The same sequence produced the AMD deal. DISH Network is the next name in the pipeline. Every litigation filing is a future licensing revenue event, not a cost.4

Pillar 3 of 3

RapidCool™ is the next toll booth — and it costs nothing in the current price

We treat RapidCool™ as a free option because it is not modelled by any sell-side firm, not guided by management in financial terms, and not required for the base case to generate a positive return. But the option value is not trivial. AI GPU racks already exceed 163kW per rack and roadmaps project 600kW/rack by 2027. At those power densities, thermal interface materials — the pastes conventionally used between heat sink and chip — become the primary bottleneck to heat dissipation. RapidCool™ applies the same direct silicon-to-silicon bonding principle as DBI® to bond a cold plate directly to the chip surface, eliminating the TIM layer. CEO Davis described improvements of approximately 70% efficiency in initial testing.13

We note that the Aeon Nimbus portfolio already includes Oracle (ORCL) explicitly tied to the AI infrastructure CapEx supercycle — $553B RPO backlog, OCI IaaS growing 84% YoY. Every data centre that Oracle builds requires HBM4 memory. Every HBM4 memory unit requires hybrid bonding. Adeia’s royalty stream is structurally downstream of the Oracle thesis’s underlying driver. The two positions are complementary at the infrastructure layer without being duplicative at the security level.

The $39 million Tessera paid for Ziptronix in 2015 is beginning to compound. The question is not whether hybrid bonding becomes the standard for HBM4 — it already is. The question is when the royalty stream becomes large enough to force a re-rating of the multiple.

The institutional case in one paragraph

Adeia holds the foundational DBI® hybrid bonding patent portfolio — the only alternative to TSMC for this technology on a global basis — at a moment when Samsung and SK Hynix are converting their HBM production lines to hybrid bonding for HBM4, when AMD has signed a multi-year logic chiplet licence, and when three to four additional major logic licences are in various stages of engagement or pending litigation. The media business, which the market uses to anchor the multiple at generic IP licensing levels, funds the debt reduction and generates cash flow while the semiconductor vertical ramps. The 73% Q4 2025 EBITDA margin is not aberrational — it is what IP licensing looks like when deals close. Entry at $30.00 on April 29, 2026. Stop at $20. Target $42.

Variant views

Variant view 1 of 3

The 2026 guidance “decline” is deliberate conservatism the street is pricing as operational deterioration

Adeia guided $395M–$435M for FY2026 against $443M in FY2025. Every quantitative screen flags this as a declining business. Four analysts who cover it maintain Buy ratings anyway. The AMD deal signed March 9 was not in FY2026 guidance issued February 23. The UMC expansion signed March 11 was not in guidance. DISH Network litigation filed April 1 — the next step in the licensing pipeline — was not in guidance. Management has explicitly said there are “multiple opportunities” that could close in 2026 that are not in the guidance.

Street: 2026 guidance implies declining revenue. FY26 consensus at $415M reflects muted growth. Market penalises apparent decline. Non-consensus: One new major deal converts the guidance “decline” into +8–12% growth. The floor is conservative by construction, not by business reality.

Variant view 2 of 3

The semiconductor vertical is worth more than Adeia’s entire current market cap if valued as a standalone AI infrastructure royalty stream

Adeia’s semiconductor revenue in FY2025 was $26M — growing 44% from $18M in FY2024. Management’s stated target is $100M in recurring semiconductor revenue. No sell-side model values the semiconductor vertical separately from the media business. They assign a blended multiple to the combined entity. At the multiple applied to comparable IP licensing businesses in semiconductor infrastructure — 18–22× revenue — the implied standalone value of the semiconductor segment at $100M revenue is $1.8–2.2B. Adeia’s current total market cap is $3.65B. The market is implying the entire media business plus semiconductor optionality above $100M is worth approximately $1.5B.

Street: Blended EV/EBITDA of ~13× applied to the whole business. No disaggregation. Media drag suppresses the AI infrastructure premium. Non-consensus: Semiconductor segment at management’s $100M target valued at semiconductor infrastructure multiples implies $1.8–2.2B standalone value — nearly half the current market cap — before the media business contributes.

Variant view 3 of 3

The DISH Network lawsuit is not a cost event — it is the next licensing revenue event, following an identical playbook to Disney and AMD

Adeia filed patent infringement litigation against DISH Network on April 1, 2026, simultaneously reiterating full-year 2026 guidance. The market read this as a litigation cost increase. We read it as the next licensing deal in pipeline form. The CEO has described the pattern explicitly: file suit → create legal pressure → resolve through long-term licence. Disney went from defendant to one of Adeia’s most important OTT licensees. AMD went from defendant to “seminal” semiconductor partner. DISH is the next name in a sequence that produces recurring revenue.

Street: Litigation increase is an operating cost headwind compressing 2026 margins. DISH outcome uncertain. Non-consensus: DISH litigation is the third application of a documented playbook that produced Disney (Q4 2025 record) and AMD (March 2026). Pattern recognition converts a cost line into a 12–18 month revenue event with high historical precedent.

Reverse DCF — what the current price requires

At ~$30 per share with approximately 111 million shares outstanding, Adeia’s market cap is approximately $3.3B. Adding net debt of approximately $290M gives enterprise value of ~$3.6B. At 12% WACC and a 3.5% terminal growth rate, this EV implies perpetual normalised EBITDA of approximately $360M — requiring sustainable EBITDA well above the guidance midpoint of $229M.

Framed correctly: it requires Adeia to reach approximately $580–600M in revenue at a 60% EBITDA margin — plausible within three to four years if one additional major logic licence converts and HBM4 royalties begin contributing. What the current price does not require is the full bull case of two logic licences plus Samsung HBM4 plus RapidCool™. It requires one logic licence and steady execution of the existing AMD and media portfolios. The bear case — where none of the logic pipeline converts and media continues declining — is what produces the $18–20 downside scenario.

Payoff asymmetry — at entry of $30

Win/loss at $30 entry: ($42 − $30) / ($30 − $20) = $12 / $10 = 1.2×. This is tighter than the ideal entry of $23–25 (which would have produced 4.5× win/loss). Entry above the target zone reflects conviction on the thesis ahead of today's binary earnings event rather than patience for a better price. The asymmetry is tighter at $30 — the thesis needs to materialise. At 2% position size vs a half-Kelly of ~6%, the position is deliberately small. We will add toward 4% if a second logic licence is announced or HBM4 royalties are confirmed.

Risks

Catalyst watchlist

Position statement — Aeon Nimbus Research

Long $ADEA at $30.00, entered April 29, 2026 — the day the stock hit its 52-week high of $30.84. Target $42.00 (+40%). Stop $20.00 (−33.3%). Initial position 2% of portfolio, with an explicit plan to add toward 4% if a second logic licence is announced or HBM4 royalties are confirmed. Q1 2026 earnings today May 4 at 5PM ET — the outcome is unknown at time of publication. This thesis is published this morning with the position already live and the timestamp clear. It joins our existing positions in Oracle (ORCL, long $143.36, target $242, stop $118, 3%), MercadoLibre (MELI, long $1,774, target $2,750, stop $1,420, 3%), and Nu Holdings (NU, long $14.53, target $21, stop $11.20, 3%). Every position at Aeon Nimbus Research — including the losses — is on the record.

[2] Adeia multi-year IP licence agreement with AMD — GlobeNewswire, March 9, 2026. “Seminal” logic chiplet deal, resolves all pending litigation, grants AMD access to hybrid bonding semiconductor IP.

[3] Adeia and UMC expand hybrid bonding collaboration — GlobeNewswire, March 11, 2026.

[4] Adeia DISH Network patent infringement litigation — GlobeNewswire, April 1, 2026. Filed in US District Court Colorado. Full 2026 guidance reiterated simultaneously.
